T: A murdered wife. A one-armed man. An obsessed detective.
D: A Chicago surgeon wrongly convicted of killing his wife escapes custody to hunt the one-armed man, with a US Marshal one step behind.
P: Serve the Italian beef when Kimble slips into Cook County Hospital as a janitor.
S: Franks on poppy seed buns, Chicago style. That train sounds like an 'L'.

Bring a pot of water to a bare simmer, add the franks and heat through without boiling. Steam or warm the rolls so they stay soft. Tuck a frank into each roll and dress in order: mustard, relish, onion, tomato wedges, a pickle spear and two peppers. Finish with a pinch of celery salt. No tomato sauce.
8 pickled sport peppers or small hot pickled chillies@Pantry
Provasic-free chicken liver pate with toast
Smooth chicken liver pâté with toast. Kimble finds Provasic damages the liver.

Melt 30g of the butter and soften the shallot, garlic and thyme. Turn up the heat, add the livers and cook until browned outside and just pink inside. Add the brandy and let it bubble off, then cool for 5 minutes. Blend with the rest of the butter and plenty of salt and pepper until silky, press into a dish and chill. Serve with the rye toast and cornichons.
M: Cook County Italian beef, dipped, with hot giardiniera
Thin Italian beef dipped in jus with hot giardiniera. Kimble poses as a Cook County janitor.

For the giardiniera, toss the capsicum, celery, carrot and chillies with a tablespoon of salt, leave 15 minutes, rinse, then cover with the vinegar and oil. Rub the beef with the garlic, oregano, chilli and fennel, sit it in a roasting dish and pour the stock around it. Roast covered at 160C until just tender, then rest and chill if you can, so it slices thinly. Slice the beef as thin as possible and warm it in the hot pan juices. Pile into the split rolls, dip the whole sandwich in the jus and top with giardiniera.
St Patrick's Day corned beef with buttered cabbage
Corned beef with buttered cabbage. Gerard loses him in the St Patrick's Day parade.

Rinse the silverside, cover with cold water and add the onion, bay, sugar and vinegar. Simmer very gently until a skewer slides in easily. Lift the beef out to rest and cook the potatoes in the liquid, adding the cabbage for the last few minutes. Drain, toss the cabbage and potatoes with the butter, warm the cream with the mustard and serve with thick slices of beef.
W: Gerard wants a donut with little sprinkles

Mix the flour, yeast, sugar and a pinch of salt, then add the milk, egg and butter and knead until smooth and springy. Cover and leave somewhere warm until doubled. Roll out 1.5cm thick, cut 8 rings and prove for 30 minutes more. Fry at 175C for a minute a side until golden, then drain. Melt the chocolate into the warm cream, dip the tops of the donuts and shower with sprinkles.
K: Big Dog pale ale from Goose Island
Cold Goose Island pale ale in chilled glasses. Never argue with the Big Dog.
Chill the beer and 4 glasses. Pour slowly with a good head.
